Part Two: Multiple Choice. Answer all five questions. Mark one letter per question, formatted "1. B".

1. A signed writing is required to enforce a sale of goods above the statutory threshold. Which party must the writing be signed by?
A. Both parties
B. The party against whom enforcement is sought
C. The party seeking enforcement
D. A neutral witness

2. Which remedy puts the injured buyer in the position performance would have?
A. Rescission
B. Expectation damages
C. Punitive damages
D. Nominal damages

3. Impracticability excuses a seller when
A. performance becomes slightly more costly
B. a basic assumption of the contract fails through no fault of the seller
C. the seller changes its mind
D. the buyer is late paying

4. Cover is
A. a reasonable substitute purchase after breach
B. an insurance policy
C. a buyer's refusal to inspect
D. a seller's right to cure

5. Consequential damages generally require
A. foreseeability at contracting
B. a jury verdict
C. a liquidated sum
D. arbitration
